thought: An electric wire took his arm at 8. He won Paralympic gold at 23. And again at 35.
support: Devendra Jhajharia, from a village in Rajasthan's Churu district, lost his left arm as a child after touching a live 11,000-volt wire while climbing a tree. He taught himself javelin with a makeshift bamboo stick and went on to win gold in the F46 javelin at the 2004 Athens Paralympics. Twelve years later, at Rio 2016, he won gold again, throwing 63.97 metres to break his own Paralympic record. He added a silver at Tokyo 2021 - three Paralympic medals across three decades, on one arm.
